en: The Therāpadāna: The Taraṇīya Thera Apadāna, Chapter Ten on the Golden Couch Once, in the city of Bārāṇasī, I was a merchant’s son named Suvanna. I saw the Buddha, the Blessed One, the Teacher, who had arrived at the city gate. Having seen him, I approached him and spoke these words: “O Sage, please enter my house. The Teacher, the Great Hero, entered my house; having sat down, he addressed me: “Suvanna, what is your wish? What do you desire? “I have no wish for wealth, nor for sons, nor for a wife. My wish is for the Dhamma; I desire the Dhamma, O Blessed One. Then the Teacher, the Great Hero, preached the Dhamma to me. Having heard the Dhamma from the Teacher, I attained the fruit of stream-entry. I then offered a golden couch to the Teacher, the Blessed One. Because of that deed, I was reborn in the delightful Tusita heaven.

From there, passing away, I was reborn in the human world. In every birth, I was wealthy and possessed of great power. For eighty-four thousand aeons, I never fell into a state of misery. I was always born into noble families, endowed with great splendor. I was handsome, fortunate, and possessed of great majesty. I was always a master of the three Vedas, skilled in all branches of knowledge. I was a teacher of the Vedas, honored by the people. I was always a king, a ruler of the earth, a lord of the four continents. I was a monarch, a wheel-turning monarch, a conqueror of the four quarters. I ruled over the whole world, possessing the seven treasures. I was a sovereign of the earth, the lord of all beings. I was always a master of the three Vedas, skilled in all branches of knowledge. “On the rugged Great Path,
a bridge has been constructed by me for the sake of the world’s crossing.”
With my own hands, full of faith,
this bridge was caused to be built by me ninety-one eons ago.
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of giving a bridge.
For fifty-five aeons,
I was once a sovereign wheel-turning monarch, possessed of great power and endowed with the seven treasures, dwelling alone in seclusion.
The four analytical knowledges...
[and so forth] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Taraṇīya spoke these verses.
This is the tenth legend of the elder Taraṇīya. The twenty-eighth chapter, the Suvaṇṇabibbohana-vagga (The Chapter on the Golden Pillows), is concluded.
